added_failures_note: the reviewed run carries no baseline_suite/after_suite pair in its manifest; derived from the two gate arms it names -- gate5-base.log (base arm, the answering change absent, 2 failed 70 passed EXIT=1) and gate5.log (head arm, 59ae0da, 72 passed EXIT=0). The head arm reported no FAILED/ERROR node id, so the added set is empty and the count is a measured 0.

findings.text: blocking: the guard swallows ProcessLookupError/PermissionError from os.getpgid and execution falls through to the identity check at reckon/crew/routing.py:3673, which raises CrewError for the same pid; reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:400 catches only ProcessLookupError, so unwatch now raises an uncaught CrewError on the watcher-exited race where it previously reported "watcher-exited", a regression the guard was not needed to introduce.

follow-on: the comment claims the dead-pid lookup "must not crash the stop that follows", but for a pid with no process the identity check at reckon/crew/routing.py:3673 raises CrewError regardless of the guard, so the guard does not prevent the crash it is justified by and no test demonstrates it prevents anything.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 512152937; ca425008 narrows terminate's identity-checked branch to a pid that still names a process and wraps the os.getpgid group lookup, and 59ae0da updates the evidence fragment prose; four files, no other change.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_worker_never_outlives_its_supervisor.py with real child processes and its declared negative control; the manifest records gate5.log (72 passed EXIT=0 at 59ae0da) and gate5-base.log (2 failed at base, including the gained reap test), so the gate the worker ran asserts the named measure.
item_verdicts.goal: the source node's goal is to extend signal_worker so a stopped or exited supervisor leaves no worker alive (prompt.txt:30); the gained commits repair terminate so a run whose recorded supervisor pid is gone while its start tick remains reaps the reparented worker (reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1787) and add a group-lookup guard (reckon/crew/routing.py:3645), though that guard's blast radius reaches six other callers.
item_verdicts.manifest: read manifest.md; it lists commits a6852ed6b..59ae0da, records the head gate (72 passed, EXIT=0) and the declared negative control at head, and names the repaired stop path as finding f580e154b17 acted at ca425008.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared write paths; git diff 512152937..59ae0da touches exactly reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py, reckon/crew/routing.py, tests/test_a_worker_never_outlives_its_supervisor.py and docs/evidence/fragments/a-run-has-one-live-writer/a-worker-never-outlives-its-supervisor.html, all inside the fence and nothing outside.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_worker_never_outlives_its_supervisor.py:285 is a real guard (it fails at base per gate5-base.log), but the reckon/crew/routing.py:3645 guard has no assertion: reverting it alone leaves the suite green because the fixed terminate no longer routes a dead pid there.
justifications.evidence: the manifest records gate5.log (72 passed, EXIT=0 at 59ae0da) with a literal command and gate5-base.log, whose red arm the harness reduces for the added-failure count.
justifications.fit: no new symbol is introduced and the change follows the surrounding idiom of reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1775, though the comment at reckon/crew/routing.py:3650 asserts a purpose the code does not achieve.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1787 now takes the identity-checked path only for a live recorded pid and reaches the run's environment mark otherwise, which is what the goal's extension needs for a gone supervisor.
justifications.reuse: the diff adds no definition; it modifies the owner of the signal capability in place (reckon/crew/routing.py:3605) rather than forking a second mechanism.
justifications.scope_discipline: all four changed paths are inside the fence, but the reckon/crew/routing.py:3645 guard changes the exception a shared helper raises for six callers beyond the node's subject.
